AITA for calling a lesbian a butch person? | I used to hate the female gender due to an abusive parent and bullying well into COLLEGE for "not belonging". But I eventually realized I was missing out on meeting some pretty cool people so I compromised with myself to give all PEOPLE a chance by removing the "female" label in my head until I got to know them a little more.

When I was dating this guy, he started hanging out with an old childhood friend that went to the same home school as us. I am 2 years younger then them so I didn't really know this person. 

Around the 5 -6th time hanging out I'm complaining about a girl from work that told me she thought I was stuck up for not immediately befriending her when I started working at the same company - she and every girl that started after us quickly became bathroom buddies. NEVER MIND that I've been nothing but nice to everyone, if a little reserved. We didn't share any interests and I'm not one for idle chatter. I let it slip that this if one of the reasons I REALLY don't like women. 

This apparently offended the friend so she asked me to describe what I thought SHE was. So I said that she was a butch person. She flipped out because 1) "butch" is a descriptor ONLY lesbians can use! 2) calling her a "person" was extremely offensive to her because someone had told her she wasn't a woman before due to her looks and orientation 3) no wonder I never spoke to her in high school! (...what? We graduated half a decade ago, what does that matter?)

I've asked a few LGBTQ people and I've been assured the use of the word butch as a descriptor was in no way derogatory. And as angry as I am that anyone had the nerve to say that to her, I think HER personal issues can't dictate what coping mechanisms I use to get by.

TL;DR: AITA for not being sensitive to this person's past trauma and calling her a person instead of a woman?

EDIT: since it keeps being brought up: when she first asked me to what she was I said a person (gender neutral for my own personal reasons so that the name and personality shine through an identified personal hang- up). When she pressed me to DESCRIBE her I added butch - a word SHE used to describe half the people at her vet's office before that day. Didn't think it changed what was said so I left it out.

EDIT 2: thanks to those of you I've spoken to I see what she was upset by. I saw the replacement of "women" with "people" as the SOLUTION to my hatred of the women due to those that made my life miserable. To her it meant something else very personal.

Don't know why it wasn't obvious to some people, but I am female.

And I did seek a counselor in college. But that was derailed when my work was destroyed by my female classmates and had to change majors to stay sane. My crime? Minding my own business and not striking up a friendship with them since I had a lot going on in my personal life that year. It's always been the females that have taken my non-interest as some sort of affront for some reason. I do the same with guys with no issue. The resentment isn't going away anytime soon, but I will keep working on it not affecting how I treat other people.
